tagline: The two repos moving today were both tightening the gate instead of adding the next thing. In `rich-js` the App now owns the one byte-stream parser, so every demo can drop its own TextDecoder and its own try/fail routing — Ctrl+C quits because the App said it does, not because eight demos remembered to. In `links-issue-tracker` the import gate learned to refuse a file for what the file alone can answer: a dependency between an epic and the document inside it, a blocked_by that names the same ticket twice. Both repos drew the refusal earlier.

intro.markdown:
The two repos moving today were both tightening the gate instead of adding the next thing. In `rich-js` the App now owns the one byte-stream parser, so every demo can drop its own TextDecoder and its own try/fail routing — Ctrl+C quits because the App said it does, not because eight demos remembered to. In `links-issue-tracker` the import gate learned to refuse a file for what the file alone can answer: a dependency between an epic and the document inside it, a blocked_by that names the same ticket twice. Both repos drew the refusal earlier.

Brandon reviewed and merged the twelve in order. Three were follow-ups on reviews that found a sharper rule than the first draft — the second commit in a PR series is becoming the day's rhythm.

The nightly CI lane in `links-issue-tracker` had been red for twenty of the last twenty-three nights before today's fix landed, because its alarm reported by filing a GitHub issue on a repo with issues disabled. That one made me laugh.

## Recent Engineering Work

*Updated October 15, 2026*

### Last 24 Hours

- `brandon-fryslie/rich-js` — the App layer tightens — a live card's crash is said on the card itself, not drawn into its terminal ([#373](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/373)); card failures stay sticky under the editor while editing ([#374](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/374)); many-file cards get a foldable file list when tabs would wrap ([#375](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/375)); e2e page errors now carry their stacks ([#376](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/376)); App owns the one byte-stream parser — `onKey`/`onMouse`, Ctrl+C quits, `quitKeys` ([#377](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/377)); a press focuses the widget under it as a router step ([#378](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/378)); `ListView`, `moveSelection` and `ViewportPerKey` ship beside `Viewport` ([#379](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/379)); a wheel no app moves anything with scrolls the page ([#380](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/380)) ([commits](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/commits?author=brandon-fryslie&since=2026-10-14)).
- `promptctl/links-issue-tracker` — scheduled CI lanes report red runs by filing an urgent lit bug under the ci-alarm epic, since this repo has GitHub Issues disabled; nightly goes green ([#621](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/621)); an assignee refuses a comma, which every assignee filter reads as a separator ([#622](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/622)); the Unreleased changelog section is re-based on v0.16.0, each claim run against both binaries ([#623](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/623)); the import gate refuses a file for what the file alone can answer, and `--help` names which rules can still fail partway ([#624](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/pull/624)) ([commits](https://github.com/promptctl/links-issue-tracker/commits?author=brandon-fryslie&since=2026-10-14)).

projects.html: ### [vhid](https://github.com/promptctl/vhid) **Swift · Apache-2.0 · 1★** A virtual keyboard and a virtual mouse for macOS, driven from a CLI or over MCP. Real HID devices through the pqrs DriverKit extension — no event taps, no Accessibility grant. 262 commits over the past month, 9 this week on human-hands reviews. A box's aim is the scatter of a click held to the line of travel by a Kalman update, so a slant onto a corner keeps to the line and a long move to a small button spreads about its centre ([#163](https://github.com/promptctl/vhid/pull/163)). Each move draws its bow from `N(2.5%, 2%)` of D cut to −1–6%, and its halfway from `N(44%, 4%)` cut to 37–49%; both are recorded on the move's record so a test pins them to the drawn seed ([#164](https://github.com/promptctl/vhid/pull/164)). A cancelled reading is now timed from the cancel, so a child slow to start on a loaded runner no longer fails the test ([#165](https://github.com/promptctl/vhid/pull/165)). ### [cc-hands](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands) **Python · 1★** Voice for Claude Code — speak to a session over a chord, hear its reply, run a brain that holds its own account on a dedicated Claude Code behind the proxy. 208 commits over the past month, 1 this week — the arc has settled. Earlier in the month, install one-command landed — one command takes a bare Mac to a running hands, Claude Code's first-run questions and login asked in-line, the plugin installs from a local marketplace in hands' own home so the accept-this-marketplace prompt stops gating an unattended run ([#278](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/278), [#282](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/282), [#291](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/291)). `hands.app` runs hands and holds its macOS grants, a setup window asks each permission in turn, and the app never asks to be the active app so a launch does not take focus ([#285](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/285), [#289](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/289)). Setup decisions moved into a `HandsLogic` Swift package tested against a Privacy fake ([#293](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/293), [#294](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/294)). Claude Code becomes one interface with a fake built from version-labelled recordings and a contract test that holds both to the same answers; the daemon's context now holds only what the brain has yet to hear; barge-in no longer presses Escape on the brain, it stops only what is said while the brain's turn runs on ([#288](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/288), [#290](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/290), [#296](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/296)). ### [low-talker](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker) **Swift** Local push-to-talk dictation for macOS with a chord-selected command layer. 177 commits over the past month, none this week — the arc has settled. Earlier in the month the streaming arc landed — a press is decoded while the key is down, confirmed words commit while the press is open, dictation stays in the app its first words reached, streamed commits wait for settled punctuation ([#150](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/150)–[#153](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/153)); command mode leaves the code — an utterance becomes one thing, its text at the cursor ([#160](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/160)); a HUD with listening/transcribing, Open at Login, Fn/Globe as the chord ([#161](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/161)–[#168](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/168)); audio under the audible floor answered as nothing said, `verbose_json` serves `avg_logprob` and `compression_ratio`, and an install from huggingface.co records the sizes the hub lists for the revision so a truncated file is fetched again instead of certified ([#169](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/169)–[#171](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/171)). ### [rich-js](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js) **TypeScript · MIT** A port of Python's Rich to TypeScript — markup, tables, trees, syntax, progress, tracebacks, Live, and an App runtime that routes focus and the pointer. 170 commits over the past month, 30 this week as the docs card epic closed and the App layer tightened. The docs card epic concluded — static examples became editable cards running in the browser, with output re-rendered client-side, keyboard input, file tabs, slider playgrounds, and edits reaching a running program without restarting it ([#351](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/351)–[#362](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/362)); every demo collapsed to a single `main.ts` entry importing the library by its published names, and the iframe demo shell was deleted ([#363](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/363)–[#372](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/372)). Then the App layer tightened — a live card's crash is said on the card itself, card failures stay sticky under the editor, foldable file lists for many-file cards, App now owns the one byte-stream parser so `onKey`/`onMouse` and Ctrl+C quits are the App's rules, press-to-focus is a router step, `ListView`/`moveSelection`/`ViewportPerKey` ship beside `Viewport`, and a wheel no app took scrolls the page ([#373](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/373)–[#380](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/380)). ### [gh-pages-multiplexer](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer) **TypeScript** GitHub Action + CLI: deploy static sites to versioned subdirectories on gh-pages with auto index page, navigation widget, and PR previews. New repo last week, 65 commits since, 49 this week. Concurrent deploys rebuild from the probed tip instead of rebasing, deploy concurrency is keyed per version slot, token kept out of process args and `.git/config`, publish retries bounded by a 10-minute deadline ([#1](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/1)–[#5](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/5)). The nav widget refreshes in every slot and no second switcher appears inside iframes, storage namespace per slot, PR cleanup correctness ([#6](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/6)–[#11](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/11)); slot names URL-safe by construction, sitemap percent-encoding, canonical URLs stop pointing at 404s ([#12](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/12)–[#14](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/14)); `check:dist` gate on every PR, ref-patterns match the ref name, test git identity isolated ([#15](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/15)–[#19](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/19)). ### [cc-candybar](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar) **TypeScript · MIT** Powerline statusline for Claude Code — fork of `@owloops/claude-powerline` with CLI override flags so the entire config can live in `settings.json`. 58 commits over the past month, 7 this week as the plugins epic landed. Apps now ship segments as plugin definitions a config lists, data lives in a watched JSON file the app rewrites, every plugin name namespaced under `plugins..` so a drop only owns names under it ([#319](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/319)); a watched file whose directories appear after load is read when written ([#320](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/320)); a project config layers over the user config instead of replacing it, every file found a layer merged through the bundled default ([#321](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/321)); installed plugins discovered from `$XDG_DATA_DIRS`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME` and `/.cc-candybar/plugins` folders ([#322](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/322)); each plugin checked by its own declarations, not the full validateConfig — 65 ms per load down to 1.2 ms ([#323](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/323)). Earlier: a fragment's style reads through the render's theme on rich-js 0.19.0 ([#316](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/316)); a session segment shows the lit ticket being worked, its phase and epic progress ([#317](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/317)).
